This game is the most fun I've ever had with the Warhammer 40k universe. If you enjoy the idea of mowing down swarms of enemies as an ultra-powered Ultramarine, then this is going to satisfy that desire better than any other. There are thousands of Orks just waiting for your bolter fire and chainsword.

It does get a little repetitive before the final act, and there are a lot of awkwardly long empty hallways to traverse, but the dev team held on to some great additions for the end of the game. Just when you've grown too tired of the same 6 or so Ork enemies the Chaos Demons show up and things get a wild change. It almost makes you miss the greenskins by the time it's over.

The game uses the aggressive heal-by-killing mechanic that makes it lean into the action, but it's not quite perfect. If they'd given some invulnerability during the takedown animation, it would have been a little more reliable, but it's hard to fault a few unwanted deaths. Likewise, despite being heavily inspired by Gears of War, there's no actual cover mechanic which would have made things a lot less awkward than trying to hide from heavy enemy fire by positioning yourself behind some crates like a chump.

Still, despite its short length, the campaign is very satisfying. It goes a little into the 40k lore, but not so much to offput newcomers. If you want a nice third-person shooter that's got a great flavor, this will easily satisfy.
The Codex Astartes supports you playing this game.
